facts.fact: Replit began rolling out Effort-Based Pricing to remaining users on July 2nd.
facts.quote: we began rolling this feature out to the remaining users last week on July 2nd.

facts.fact: Replit offered $10 in free credits to all members who used the new Effort-Based Pricing model.
facts.quote: we would like to offer $10 in free Replit credits to all Replit members who used the new pricing model

facts.fact: A cost calculation error on July 11th incorrectly computed Replit checkpoint charges, impacting approximately 6% of paying users, according to Replit.
facts.quote: This impacted approximately 6% of paying users.

facts.fact: Under the previous pricing model, Agent v1 billed a flat rate of $0.25 per checkpoint.
facts.quote: bill the user a flat rate of $0.25, which at the time was enough to cover the cost of AI and running the service.

facts.fact: With Effort-Based Pricing, simpler requests may cost as little as $0.06 per checkpoint.
facts.quote: Simpler requests may cost as little as $0.06 and more involved requests will usually cost more than $0.25

facts.fact: Under the earlier approach, Agent generated a checkpoint every ninth time it ran a command behind the scenes.
facts.quote: we patched the Agent to generate a checkpoint every ninth time that the Agent ran a command behind the scenes.

facts.fact: Under Effort-Based Pricing, Agent creates at most one checkpoint per request.
facts.quote: Agent will create at most one checkpoint per request instead of many.

facts.fact: Replit rolled out an AI model usage efficiency change to all users by the end of July 7th.
facts.quote: We quickly rolled these changes out to all users by the end of July 7th.

facts.fact: Shortly after launching its new pricing, Replit identified a double-digit percent efficiency win in its AI model usage (vendor's own claim).
facts.quote: we identified a major double-digit percent efficiency win in our AI model usage

facts.fact: Replit states that users had been accustomed to seeing $0.25 charges per checkpoint.
facts.quote: When users are accustomed to seeing $0.25 charges per checkpoint, it’s harder to interpret a $0.75 checkpoint

facts.fact: Replit cites a $0.75 checkpoint as an example of a newer checkpoint that can include the work of three $0.25 checkpoints.
facts.quote: even if that $0.75 checkpoint includes the work of three $0.25 checkpoints.

facts.fact: Under Replit's Effort-Based Pricing, chat cost with the Agent is summed into the next checkpoint's charges.
facts.quote: Even more surprising is that the chat cost is summed in the next checkpoint's charges.

facts.fact: Replit states that Effort-Based Pricing ties user-facing charges to its operational costs.
facts.quote: Because Effort-Based Pricing ties user-facing charges to Replit operational costs, users began to see cost savings immediately.
